desc.features: What {{BRAND_NAME}} does on the computer, on Android and as a web app on iPhone, with a table for every feature and device.
desc.privacy: Which connections {{BRAND_NAME}} makes and why. Your data stays on your device, and with an account also as an encrypted copy that only your devices can read.
desc.download: Download {{BRAND_NAME}} for free for Mac, Windows, Linux and Android, or open it as a web app on iPhone, with instructions for every device.
desc.about: {{BRAND_NAME}} is a student project from Brandenburg. Why the app exists and what you may do with it.

areas.title: Timetable
areas.text: Week A and B, double periods, single periods or your own times. {{BRAND_NAME}} shows the current and next lesson with the room.

areas.title: Grades
areas.text: Points from 0 to 15 or grades from 1 to 6, depending on your year. {{BRAND_NAME}} works out each subject's average, exams count a third.

areas.title: Homework and tests
areas.text: Homework, tests and exams with a countdown. Tasks get a due date and one of three priorities.

areas.title: IServ
areas.text: Sign in once with your IServ account. {{BRAND_NAME}} then fetches your assignments on its own, and on the computer your IServ mail too. You get the substitution plan as a PDF or image if your school shows it on an IServ info screen. On Android, events come in as well, and new messages show up as notifications.

areas.title: Transit
areas.text: Connections with live delays and platforms. The way to school and back home is one tap away.

areas.title: Calendar
areas.text: Your own events and the school holidays and public holidays of all 16 German states, without typing them in. On the computer, {{BRAND_NAME}} syncs your events with your Google Calendar both ways and, if you like, adds your timetable and tests to a calendar of its own, “{{BRAND_NAME}} Schule”. On Android, events from IServ come in too.

areas.title: Luna
areas.text: Luna is the assistant in {{BRAND_NAME}}. Ask her what is on tomorrow, tell her „Maths p. 38 for Monday“ and she adds the homework. Before an exam she builds you a study plan.
facts: Answers from your timetable, tasks and grades
Adds tasks and homework from a sentence

macos: On first launch macOS blocks the app because it isn't signed by Apple. Go to System Settings, Privacy & Security, and click “Open Anyway”.
steps.macos_terminal: Or paste this into Terminal, the script installs the app into /Applications:
windows: If your browser warns that the file is rarely downloaded, choose “Keep”.
If Windows SmartScreen warns you, click “More info” and “Run anyway”.
{{BRAND_NAME}} installs without admin rights and opens by itself.
linux: Double-click the .deb file to install {{BRAND_NAME}} through your software center, or run this in your Downloads folder: sudo apt install ./{{BRAND_NAME}}-*.deb
Then open {{BRAND_NAME}} from your app menu.
android: Open the APK and allow installs from this source.
If your Samsung phone blocks the install, briefly turn off Auto Blocker under Settings › Security and privacy.
{{BRAND_NAME}} tells you when an update is ready.
ios: Open the web app in Safari.
There, tap Share {share}, then “Add to Home Screen”.
From now on, start {{BRAND_NAME}} from the new icon and set it up there. What you enter in the Safari tab doesn't carry over.
web: Open the link and {{BRAND_NAME}} runs right in your browser.
Your data lives in this browser's storage.

privacy_page.lock_text: {{BRAND_NAME}} stores your IServ and mail login details encrypted, on the computer with Fernet and a key from 600,000 PBKDF2 rounds, on Android in the system's encrypted storage. On the computer, {{BRAND_NAME}} encrypts grades, homework, tests, exams, presentations, events, notes, mail drafts, saved places and your history with Luna the same way. Not encrypted there are the timetable with subjects, teachers, rooms and times, the task list, training, Pomodoro statistics, reviews, bookmarks, tickets, the cached substitution plan and the settings with your birthday and weather location, and on Android and in the web app everything except the login details. Without an account, all of it stays on your device. With an account, {{BRAND_NAME}} encrypts your timetable, first name and profile picture with AES-256 before uploading them. The key comes from your password and never leaves the device, so the server cannot read the entries.
privacy_page.lock_number_label: PBKDF2 rounds for your login details on the computer
no: Tracking, usage analytics or crash reports
privacy_page.open_title: You don't have to take my word for it
privacy_page.open_text: Anyone can read the source code of the app. Every line that touches your data on your device is public on GitHub.

download_page.lede: {{BRAND_NAME}} stays free, even once the beta is over. You don't need an account; you can start right after the download.

faq.a: No. {{BRAND_NAME}} is free for you, and its source code is public on GitHub. There are no paid features or subscriptions.

faq.q: Do I have to type in my timetable?
faq.a: Yes, once. {{BRAND_NAME}} can't fetch it from IServ or WebUntis. The setup in the app walks you through it in a few minutes, and if someone in your course has already entered the plan, they can send it to you. Then you only change what's different for you.

faq.q: I already have IServ and WebUntis. What does {{BRAND_NAME}} add?
faq.a: IServ and WebUntis each know only their own part. {{BRAND_NAME}} shows you on one screen which lesson is next and in which room, and what's left to do before your next test. {{BRAND_NAME}} doesn't know about cancellations in WebUntis, you still see those there.
On Android, the Mac, Windows and Linux, {{BRAND_NAME}} tells you when a new version is out. You download it here.

faq.q: Why isn't {{BRAND_NAME}} in the App Store or on Google Play?
faq.a: I distribute {{BRAND_NAME}} directly, without store fees and with faster updates. That's why the iPhone gets the web app.

faq.q: Can I move my data to a new device?
faq.a: Yes, with a backup. In the settings under Daten (data), you save your timetable and subjects, grades, homework, tests, exams, presentations, tasks, events, notes, places and settings to a file and read it in on the new device. You set up training, bookmarks and your IServ and mail logins there again. With an account, your timetable, first name and profile picture reach your other devices by themselves, encrypted. For everything else there is the backup.
No. {{BRAND_NAME}} is an independent student project. It only uses your IServ account to sign in on your behalf.
Not yet. The app itself is in German, it was built for German schools.

about_page.title: A student project from Brandenburg
about_page.lede: {{BRAND_NAME}} is built by a student from Brandenburg, currently in the final years of school. The app started as a tool for their own school day and is now there for anyone looking for something similar.
story: For school, my calendar, the bus and my homework I had a separate app each. None of them knew about the others.
{{BRAND_NAME}} brings that together: the timetable knows which room is next, tests sit with a countdown among your deadlines, and the bus home is one tap away.
Everything runs on your device. I don't want to see your grades, and I can't.

privacy_policy.s1_p1: The data controller within the meaning of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) is:
privacy_policy.s2_p1: {{BRAND_NAME}} was built on a "Local-First" principle. This means: All data you enter in the App is stored on your device. An account is optional. Without an account, the App transmits your entries to no server of the Provider. With an account, it uploads a copy of your timetable, first name and profile picture, which it encrypts on your device first, see Section 3 f). Third-party services receive data only when you use a feature that needs them, such as transit or weather. The App also makes some requests by itself, for example to check for updates. Section 3 lists these services.
privacy_policy.s2_p2: The Provider processes personal data through the App only if you create an account (Section 3 f). Otherwise data goes only to the services a feature needs (e.g., real-time public transit data), or to those listed in Section 3 d) when the App makes a request by itself.
privacy_policy.s3_sub1_p1: All data you enter (timetables, grades, tasks, training data, notes, etc.) is stored on your device. With an account, an encrypted copy of your timetable, first name and profile picture comes along, see f). The App stores login details, for example for IServ and email, in encrypted form. In the apps for computers, this also applies to grades, homework, tests, exams, presentations, events, notes, mail drafts, saved places and the assistant's history. Stored unencrypted in a local database there are the timetable with subjects, teachers, rooms and times, the task list, training data, Pomodoro statistics, reviews, bookmarks, tickets and the settings, which include your birthday and weather location. The cached substitution plan is also stored there unencrypted. On Android and in the web app, all data except the login details is stored unencrypted. The Provider has no access to this data at any time. This also applies to the encrypted copy in the account, see f).
privacy_policy.s3_sub2_p1: When you use the transit feature, the App sends requests to Transitous (api.transitous.org) and, for ticket prices in Berlin and Brandenburg, to transport.rest (v6.vbb.transport.rest). These requests contain the stops, addresses and times of your search. If you have saved your home or your school as a place, connections from or to there also include its location, and “In der Nähe” (nearby) includes your current location if you allow it. In the older views of the computer app, requests also go to transport.rest and, for fares, to Deutsche Bahn. No device IDs are transmitted.
privacy_policy.s3_sub2_p2: If you have saved your school and your home as places, the App also asks Transitous by itself for the next connections from school to home when you open a page of the App between 90 minutes before your last lesson ends and two hours after. This includes the location of both places.
privacy_policy.s3_sub3_p1: {{BRAND_NAME}} contains no analytics, no tracking, no crash reporters, and no telemetry. No usage statistics are collected whatsoever.
privacy_policy.s3_sub4_p1: The App contacts the following services when you use the feature in question. It makes the requests marked “by itself” without any action on your part. As with any connection, the service sees your IP address.
privacy_policy.s3_list1: Your school's IServ: your username and password to sign in, then the requests for mail, substitution plan, assignments, events and messages (not in the web app)
privacy_policy.s3_list2: Your email provider: login details and mail, directly via IMAP and SMTP (apps for computers)
privacy_policy.s3_list3: Open-Meteo: the place you want the weather for, or the location of your home
privacy_policy.s3_list4: Holiday services (feiertage-api.de, schulferien-api.de, ferien-api.de, date.nager.at): your federal state
privacy_policy.s3_list5: Wikipedia: the term you ask the assistant about
privacy_policy.s3_list6: Anthropic: your question to the assistant and the data from the App it needs to answer, only if you enter your own Claude key (apps for computers)
privacy_policy.s3_list7: Hugging Face and GitHub: the download of the assistant's language model
privacy_policy.s3_list8: PyPI: the download of the Python packages on the Mac app's first start on Intel Macs and after updates
privacy_policy.s3_list9: This website: the request for the latest version, at start and then every two hours (by itself, apps for computers and Android)
privacy_policy.s3_list11: The websites of your bookmarks: a request to the page, to show its logo next to the bookmark
privacy_policy.s3_list12: This website or GitHub: the download of the new version of the App when you tap “Aktualisieren” (update) in the App (Android)
privacy_policy.s3_list13: Google: your calendar and, where set up, Gmail, when you connect your Google account (apps for computers), see e)
privacy_policy.s3_list14: {{BRAND_NAME}} account at Cloudflare: your email address, a check value for your password and your encrypted entries, only if you create an account or are signed in, see f)
privacy_policy.s3_list15: Google (Gmail): your email address and the code, when you create an account or reset your password, see f)
privacy_policy.s3_sub5_p1: In the apps for computers you can connect your Google account. {{BRAND_NAME}} then reads your calendar events and the list of your calendars through Google's APIs and adds the events you create or change in the App. If you switch on “Stundenplan und Tests in Google eintragen” (add timetable and tests to Google), the App creates a calendar of its own for this and edits only that one. The App reaches Gmail through the Google sign-in only in installations set up for it. There it can read your mail, send mail on your behalf and delete it. Otherwise you connect Gmail with an app password through your email provider, as described in d).
privacy_policy.s3_sub5_p2: The App uses this data only to show it to you on your device and to let you edit it there. What you change, it writes back to your Google account. It stores a copy of the calendar events and the Google sign-in encrypted on your device. The App does not pass this data on to the provider's servers or to third parties, and it does not use it for advertising.
privacy_policy.s3_sub5_p3: If you disconnect your Google account in the App under Einstellungen, Konten (Settings, Accounts), it deletes the sign-in and the copy on your device. You can revoke the access itself at any time at [myaccount.google.com/permissions](https://myaccount.google.com/permissions).
privacy_policy.s3_sub5_p4: {{BRAND_NAME}}'s use and transfer of information received from Google APIs to any other app will adhere to the [Google API Services User Data Policy](https://developers.google.com/terms/api-services-user-data-policy), including the Limited Use requirements.
privacy_policy.s3_sub6_p1: From version 0.6 you can create an account. With it, {{BRAND_NAME}} keeps your timetable (subjects, teachers, rooms, lesson times and A/B weeks), your first name and your profile picture the same on all your devices. The account is optional, and the App works the same without it. The Provider runs the service for it at Cloudflare (Cloudflare, Inc., USA). The database is kept in data centres in the EU. The requests of your devices pass through Cloudflare's network. Cloudflare is certified under the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework. More in [Cloudflare's privacy policy](https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/).
privacy_policy.s3_sub6_p2: For your account, the service stores:
privacy_policy.s3_list16: your email address and when you created and confirmed the account
privacy_policy.s3_list17: a check value for your password. The password itself never leaves your device: the App derives a sign-in key from it with 600,000 PBKDF2 rounds, and the service stores only an HMAC of that key
privacy_policy.s3_list18: your encrypted entries: the last 20 versions of your timetable and the last 3 versions of your first name and profile picture, each with its size and time of arrival. The service deletes older versions as soon as a new one arrives
privacy_policy.s3_list19: a session for each signed-in device, stored only as a check value. It is valid for 30 days and ends at once when you sign out, reset your password or delete your account
privacy_policy.s3_list20: the six-digit codes for confirming and resetting, only as an HMAC. A code is valid for 10 minutes
privacy_policy.s3_list21: counters against abuse: how often codes, sign-ups, sign-ins, deletion attempts and entries were requested within a window of at most one hour, each tied to your email address, your account or the IP address of the request
privacy_policy.s3_sub6_p3: The App encrypts your entries on your device with AES-256-GCM before it uploads them. It derives the key from your password, and the key never leaves the device. The service therefore cannot read what your timetable, first name or profile picture say. It only sees which account an entry belongs to, whether it belongs to the timetable or the profile, roughly how large it is (in steps of 1 KiB), when it arrived and how often your account sends entries. As with any connection, Cloudflare and the service also see your device's IP address.
privacy_policy.s3_sub6_p4: The service sends the code for confirming your email address and for resetting your password through Gmail from the account horaapp.team@gmail.com. Google receives your email address, the code and the text of the mail. Gmail keeps every mail it sends in that account's Sent folder, and if a mail cannot be delivered, the account receives the bounce. The service puts the mail together at Cloudflare and does not store it, and it keeps the code only as an HMAC. More in [Google's privacy policy](https://policies.google.com/privacy).
privacy_policy.s3_sub6_p5: On your device, the App keeps your email address, the session key and the key for your entries for the account. They belong to this device only and go into no backup file.
privacy_policy.s3_sub6_p6: Your confirmed account with its email address, check value and entries stays until you delete it. Signing out deletes nothing in the cloud. If you reset your password, the service deletes all entries and ends all sessions, and your devices upload their data again afterwards. The service clears everything else every hour, with these deadlines: an account that was never confirmed 7 days after its last sign-up, at the latest one hour later or, if a code for it is still valid then, one hour after that code expires; a code as soon as it is used or replaced, otherwise at the latest about 2 hours after it was sent; a session at the latest one hour after its 30 days run out; the counters against abuse at the latest 2 hours after their window started; the daily count of all code mails together, which holds no personal data, after one day and one hour at the latest.
privacy_policy.s3_sub6_p7: Two things lie outside these deadlines. The database at Cloudflare keeps a history for 7 days from which an earlier state can be restored (D1 Time Travel), so deleted data remains in that history for up to 7 days. And the code mails stay in the Sent folder of the Gmail account until the Provider deletes them there.
privacy_policy.s3_sub6_p8: With “Konto löschen” (delete account) in the App's settings you can delete your account yourself at any time. You enter your password, and as at sign-in the App sends the service only the sign-in key derived from it. The service then deletes your account, all entries, all sessions, your codes and the counters tied to your email address and your account at once. Counters tied only to the IP address of a request go with the others after 2 hours at the latest. Your devices keep their data and sign out at their next request.
privacy_policy.s3_sub6_p9: Cloudflare sets the headers “NEL” and “Report-To” (Network Error Logging) in the service's answers. Browsers that support them report errors in connecting to the service to Cloudflare, such as the kind of error, the address requested and the time, and Cloudflare sees the IP address. Successful connections are not reported.
privacy_policy.s3_sub6_p10: The legal basis for the account, the sync and the code mails is Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR, as you create the account to use this service. The counters against abuse and the other protective measures rest on Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR. The legitimate interest is to protect the service and the accounts against misuse.

privacy_policy.s4_p2: This data is collected solely to ensure operation and prevent misuse (legal basis: Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR, legitimate interest) and is automatically deleted after a short period. No identification of individual persons takes place.
privacy_policy.s4_p3: The Website is hosted by Netlify (Netlify, Inc., 101 2nd Street, San Francisco, CA 94105, USA). Netlify may also process the access data listed above in the USA. day.text: Good morning. Chemistry in B206 next.

start.free_lesson: At school they teach you: if an app is free, you are the product.
start.free_text: I get nothing from you, no money and no data. I build {{BRAND_NAME}} for fun and out of conviction: a school app does not belong behind a paywall, and your data belongs neither to advertisers nor to anyone else. It belongs to you. That is why it stays on your device, and not even I can get to it.
